writtenBefore: any 2025 data was fetched or looked at; committed before the fetch so git history shows the order
question: Can the Top 25 Pick 'em model predict the next AP poll's order better, without overfitting, by changing at most three settings?

tuning.transitions: every consecutive pair of regular-season AP polls (poll week N -> poll week N+1), scored with poll week N's games
tuning.source: CFBD /rankings (seasonType=regular), /games (seasonType=regular, classification=fbs), /lines (seasonType=regular); fetched once, cached in data/pickem-history/2025-raw.json
tuning.line: first provider found in ['consensus','DraftKings','ESPN Bet','Bovada','Caesars'], else the first listed (same order as scripts/fetch-cfb-data.mjs); formattedSpread parsed with src/utils/spread.js
tuning.opponentQualityStandIn: an unranked opponent's quality uses its rank by pre-game Elo among FBS teams that week (a team with no game that week keeps its latest earlier postgame Elo); live 2026 data uses SP+ rank here
tuning.computerRankStandIn: a team's own computer rank is that Elo rank alone (live 2026 data averages SP+/FPI/Elo ranks)
tuning.qualityWins: wins through week N over opponents ranked 20 or better in the AP poll in force for that game's week (scripts/lib/game-log.mjs QUALITY_WIN_MAX_RANK)
tuning.outcome: src/utils/pickemModel.js autoResultFor on the final score (blowout = 14+)
tuning.twoGamesInOneWeek: use the later game by start date; count reported
tuning.alignmentCheck: for every transition, ranked teams that lost that week must on average fall in the next poll (exits count as #26); otherwise the builder stops

metric.name: weighted pairwise order errors
metric.pairs: every pair of teams in poll week N; teams missing from poll N+1 are tied just below it; a pair of two such teams is skipped; entrants are not scored
metric.D_base: pairs whose order really changed (the leave-the-poll-unchanged baseline's errors)
metric.D_model: pairs the projection puts in a different order than poll N+1
metric.objective: E = sum over transitions of weight x D_model (lower is better)
metric.skill: 1 - sum(weight x D_model) / sum(weight x D_base)
metric.alsoReported: root movers (longest-increasing-subsequence method, unchanged-rank rule for ties) and their mean absolute rank error, for continuity with the weekly docs

baseModel: PARAMS_V1 in scripts/lib/pickem-model-params.mjs, test-pinned to production src/utils/projectTop25.js

candidates.meaning: extra drop (rank slots) for a loss to a team outside poll week N
drift += k x clamp(actual margin - line's expected margin, +/-21) for final games with a line; a loss still can't be net positive

fitting: a setting is fit on a set of transitions by taking the grid value with the lowest E; ties go to the value nearest noChange

passRules.R1_crossValidation: hold out each 2025 transition in turn, fit on the rest, score the held-out one; the summed held-out improvement over the base model must be > 0 and its 5th percentile over 10,000 bootstrap resamples of transitions (seed 20260923) must be > 0
passRules.R2_stability: fit separately on 2025 transitions out of poll weeks 3-8 and out of poll weeks 9+; neither may land on noChange, and the two must be at most one grid step apart or within 2x of each other measured as distance from noChange
passRules.R3_carriesTo2026: at the reported value, weighted D_model over the three 2026 transitions must not exceed the base model's
passRules.R4_notOneTeam: at the reported value, the 2025 improvement must stay > 0 after removing every pair involving any single team, for each team in turn
passRules.R5_reportedValue: over all 2025 transitions, take the best grid value; report the value nearest noChange whose E is no more than the best's plus one bootstrap standard error of their paired per-transition difference

forwardSelection: round 1 tests each setting on the base model; the passing setting with the largest summed held-out improvement (R1) is kept at its reported value; later rounds test the remaining settings on top of it; stop when none passes or after 3 settings
notTested: line terms that treat wins and losses differently or depend on rank
